 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 30.11.2020 passed by the Court of III Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (SCCH-18) in MVC.No.1211/2019.

entities.text: Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (SCCH-18)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meagre compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the appellant seeks an enhancement of compensation.
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both parties.

3. The appellant filed this appeal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of NC: 2024:KHC:27350 Rs.30,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty Lakhs only) on account of injuries sustained by the claimant in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05.02.2019.

It is alleged that on the said date at about 1.30 p.m, when the claimant was proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-53-EU-5638, when he reached near Greenwood High School on Varthur-Sarjapur Main Road, at that point of time one JCB bearing registration No.KA-51-MC-3961,
which was parked by the side of the road, and the driver of the said vehicle suddenly turned his vehicle negligently towards the right side of the road without giving any indication and hit the claimant Motorcycle, due to which the claimant sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to the hospital and took treatment as an inpatient, due to which he is suffering from fracture and disability.
Hence, prayed for compensation.
4. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 was placed ex-parte.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed a statement of objections, denying the rash and NC: 2024:KHC:27350 negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and also contended that this accident occurred purely due to the negligence of the rider of the Motorcycle.
Hence, prays for the dismissal of the appeal.

5. Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
Kantharaj.V vs A Shankar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45331826/
2 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the JCB bearing registration No.KA-51-MC-3961?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. To prove the case, the appellant himself was examined as PW.1 and the Doctor as PW.2 and 13 documents were marked as Exs.P1 to P13.
The respondents have not led any evidence or marked any documents.

After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.5,25,547/- by fixing a Contributory Negligence of 20% towards the claimant and 80% towards the Insurance Company under various heads as under:
SL.

Compensation Heads Compensation No. Amount in Rs.
1 Towards Pain and 35,000-00 suffering 2 Towards Loss of 20,000-00 amenities 3
Towards Nourishment, 15,000-00 conveyance and attendant charges 4
Towards Medical 1,51,687-00 expenses 5
Towards loss of future 2,55,360-00 income 6
Towards Loss of income 28,500-00 during laid-up period and rest period 7
Future medication 20,000-00 Total 5,25,547-00 8.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

Learned counsel for the appellant has contended that the Tribunal committed an error in fixing Contributory Negligence on the part of the claimant, when there is no evidence adduced by the respondents.
The Charge sheet was also filed against the JCB driver.

Hence, he prayed for fixing the liability on the Insurance Company and also contended that the Tribunal committed an error in taking the lowest income and that the multiplier was not adopted properly.
Hence, prayed for an enhancement of the compensation amount.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company supported the judgment passed by the Tribunal and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
11. On perusal of the records, which reveal as per the evidence of PW.1, the eyewitness and the injured have categorically stated that this accident occurred when he was proceeding on the road.

Kantharaj.V vs A Shankar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45331826/
3
The JCB, which was NC: 2024:KHC:27350 parked on the left side of the road, all of a sudden moved on the right side without any indication, due to which the accident occurred.
The police, after registering the FIR and investigating the matter, filed the Charge sheet against the JCB driver, and the Charge sheet was not challenged by the driver of the JCB.
The owner also did not contest the matter before the Tribunal by leading evidence to show there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the JCB.
Even the respondent/Insurance Company did not summon the driver to examine before the Court to prove there is Contributory Negligence on the part of the rider/claimant.
Considering the same view, the Tribunal committed an error in holding there was a Contributory Negligence on the part of the rider/claimant.
12. On the other hand, this accident occurred when the driver of the JCB, rode the vehicle without any indication by taking the road side.

Therefore, the finding on issue No.1 is hereby modified,
holding that this NC: 2024:KHC:27350 accident occurred purely because of the negligence of the driver of the JCB.
13. As regards the computation of compensation, the accident occurred on 05.02.2019.
The age of the claimant was 41 years and he was admitted to the hospital for a period of 15 days.
Thereafter, he had taken further treatment as an outpatient and his patella was fractured.
The doctor has assessed the disability of 52% to the left lower limb and 26% to the whole body.
He has suffered a lot of pain and agony.

Therefore, I deem it just and appropriate to award Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and agony'.
14.
Towards 'Food, Nourishment and attendant charges', the Tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/-.
The same is retained.
15. Towards 'medical expenses', the Tribunal awarded Rs.1,51,687/- based on the medical bills.
The same is retained.
The income taken by the Tribunal is Rs.9,500/- p.m, but in the Lok adalath for the accident year 2019, Rs.14,000/- is to be considered.
Therefore, the income to be considered is Rs.14,000/- p.m.
The appellant is entitled to a 3 month laid-up period.
Hence, the appellant is entitled to an amount of Rs.42,000/- (Rs.14,000x3) under the head 'loss of income during the laid-up period'.

17. The disability assessed by the Doctor is 52% to the left lower limb and 26% to the whole body,
but the Tribunal considered only 16%.
Therefore, I propose to take 18% of disability be considered for the whole body.

Therefore, 'loss of future income' would be Rs.4,23,360/- (Rs.14,000 x 12 x 14 x 18%).
18.
Towards 'loss of amenities', the Tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/-.
The same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
- 10 - Kantharaj.

V vs A Shankar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45331826/
4 NC: 2024:KHC:27350 19.

In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.7,02,047/- as against Rs.5,25,547/- as mentioned in the table below:
 SL.

Heads Amount in  No. Rs.
 1 Pain and agony 40,000-00  2 Food, Nourishment and 15,000-00  attendant charges
3 Medical expenses 1,51,687-00  4 Loss of income during 42,000-00  laid-up period
5 Loss of future income 4,23,360-00  6 Loss of amenities 30,000-00  Total 7,02,047-00 20.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER I.

The appeal is allowed-in-part;
II.

The judgment and award dated 30.11.2020 Passed in MVC.No.1211/2019 by the III Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes,
Bengaluru (SCCH-18) is modified;

Bengaluru (SCCH-18)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
III. The claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.7,02,047/- as - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:27350 against Rs.5,25,547/- awarded by the Tribunal;
IV.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal at the rate of 8% per annum on the compensation amount of Rs.5,25,547/- is left undisturbed.
The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum;

V. The entire compensation amount shall be paid by respondent/Insurance Company within sixty days from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment;
VI. 40% of the award amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through e-payment.

Sd/-
JUDGE AM Kantharaj.
